Right printed page: only a cropped sliver at the right edge, with the first few letters of its lines visible and no readable text.

main_text.p: maiores occasiones probandæ virtutis suppeditaret. Ait ergò, Rex est qui præ-sidentiam in nos suscepit, Christus Domini est, non ab humano honore, sed à cœlesti iudicio sumpto honorifico testimonio, contemnis conseruum tuum sed reuerere Dominum, aspernaris electum ? metue eum qui elegit; nec pepercit tantum; sed & excusationem pro eo composuit, nec permisit, ut alij occiderent; sed perinde ac si aliquod depositum suæ fidei concreditum accepisset, pro quo rationem effet redditurus non attigit, alios coercuit Satelles optimus & custos corporis pro hoste factus; Etenim si vulgares istos Principes ab Imperatore designatos, etiamsi sint improbi, si fures, si prædones, si iniusti, si denique, quodcunque aliud fuerint, timemus cum horrore, non propter malitiam despicientes eos, sed propter dignitatem illius à quo electi sunt reuerentes, multo amplius id facere conuenit in his quos elegit Deus, nondum Deus abdicauit illum Principatu, nondum fecit eum ex Rege Priuatum. Itaq; ne inuertamus ordinem, neq; rebellemus Deo, Apostolicum illud dictum factis præstantes, quoniam quis-

page.notes: Right printed page is cropped at the scan edge; only the first letters of its lines are visible (qui, oni, ret, mu, dei, ille, lat, eu, er, pl, A, m, nt, cc, at, ca, te, at, n, c), so no reliable text could be transcribed from it. The outer blank column at left holds no text. The catchword "quis-" is printed at the right below the last line. Reading of "præ-" in the italic heading word is uncertain; the printed form looks like "pr&-" and may be a ligature for præ-. Some italic/roman boundaries in the long sentence may be uncertain at this resolution.
